messages:
mia (AE): Quantus asked for a compact perf check. Requirements: sustained 90 qps chat (total seq ~512), short spikes to 600 qps, and an SLO table for p95/p99/p99.9 comparing redwood-7b-fp32 vs redwood-7b-4bit. They want reproducible CI steps and a short security note on prompt retention.

jun (SRE): Plan: 10m warm, 40m steady @90qps, bursts: 3m@300, 2m@450, 5m@600, 10m cooldown. Capture p50/p95/p99/p99.9, gpu slice util, batch size distribution, kv-cache hit ratio. Tag runs: customer=quantus bench=multi-sla.

ara (SE): Using seq_in 128 / seq_out 384 -> 512 total. Recommend target batch sizes: 4bit=8, fp32=16. For repeated 600 qps bursts advise Dedicated or reserved burst capacity; otherwise enable routing fallback.

zach (Solutions Eng): Quick cost sketch: assume avg output 70 tok/resp. For steady 90 qps that's ~6.3k tok/s. Rough per-token: fp32 ~ $0.0000010, 4bit ~ $0.00000035 (list-rate examples). I'll produce a spreadsheet with run-specific totals.

jun (SRE): CI command (pasteable):
```bash
./bench/run_bench.sh \
  --model redwood-7b-4bit \
  --profile profiles/quantus_multi_sla.json \
  --duration 4200 \
  --out gs://redwood-temp/quantus/run-4bit.json \
  --meta "customer=quantus,env=bench" \
  --redact-prompts true
```
Redact flag hashes inputs; we keep only hashes + token counts for compliance. Profile will be uploaded to gs://redwood-temp/quantus/profiles/.

ci-bot: job quantus-bench-v1 queued on runner-us-west-2 (id: ci-quantus-2024-07-15)

jun (SRE): interim: finished steady 40m @90qps on 4bit. p95 ~160ms, p99 ~390ms, p99.9 ~780ms. gpu_util ~60%, median batch 8. Partial upload: gs://redwood-temp/quantus/interim-4bit.json

ara (SE): Looks reasonable for 4bit steady. Please run fp32 next with same profile.

jun (SRE): final: both model runs complete. Topline: 4bit steady p95 165ms, burst@600 p95 520ms, burst@600 p99.9 1.1s. fp32 steady p95 100ms, burst@600 p95 240ms, burst@600 p99.9 700ms. Observed cost delta ~3.0x fp32 vs 4bit for per-token compute.

zach (Solutions Eng): Recommendation: For strict tail SLAs choose fp32 on Dedicated or increase slice count during known bursts. For cost-sensitive steady traffic choose 4bit and enable automatic fallback/routing policy for bursts. I'll attach a cost appendix and commit discount scenarios.

mia (AE): Great. Action items: jun upload final profiles + redact proof (gs://redwood-temp/quantus/final/), ara draft one-pager + TL;DR, zach finalize cost sheet, mia prepare deck for Fri meeting 11am PT. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
